problem: The formula gives only the moment-induced bolt force. An eccentric tensile load F also produces a direct tensile share F/n in every bolt. The section tells students to add only the moment term to preload, so the total external bolt tension is understated and the force balance is incomplete.
fix: State the total external tensile force on bolt i as F/n + M y_i/Σy_i², with M = F e and signed y_i measured from the neutral axis. Add this total external tensile force to the preload when checking the tension-side bolt.

problem: The example says the two bolts at (50, 100) and (50, −100) give the largest secondary shear. All four corner bolts have r = 111.8 mm, so all four have the same secondary shear magnitude. Singling out two can mislead students.
fix: Say that all four bolts have r = 111.8 mm and equal secondary shear magnitude. After vector addition, the largest resultant occurs at the two bolts at x = +50 for the assumed clockwise moment.

problem: The symbol F_i is used for preload in Section 2 and again for bolt tensile force in Section 4. The same symbol for two different quantities is confusing when adding them.
fix: Keep F_i for preload. Use F_b,i or F_t,i for the bolt tensile force in Section 4.
